q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of a brass bathroom tap?
title: Brass tap carbon footprint per piece
short: Weigh the brass casting or forging per tap, including runners and machining swarf, and multiply by the brass supplier's figure. Add melting, machining, polishing and chrome plating energy, then divide the unit's energy by taps passed.

ul: Brass ingot or rod by weight, including runners.
Melting furnace fuel or induction power.
Swarf and rejects returned to melting.

p: Report per tap with its finished weight. Swarf that goes back to the furnace is not a loss, so do not count it twice.

example.title: Worked example: brass tap unit per piece (one month)
lines: Plant total: 34,550 / 50,000 = 0.691 kg CO2 per piece
Add brass and plating chemicals for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
